title: Typed Frobenius-power pasting for compactification exchange on systems
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Supply one compactification $c_0=(j_0,p_0)$ over $k_0$, and write $X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY$ for its base change, with $f=pj$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $W=X,\overline X,Y$ let $g_W=\operatorname{id}_{W_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ be geometric Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and put $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be strict semilinear $B_{W,n}$-module systems, with simultaneous derived operations on $D(\mathscr S_W)$ [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For every $r\geq1$ write $G_{W,r}=(g_W^r)^{-1}$ on these systems, transported along the constant coefficient isomorphisms; let
$$t^W_m:G_{W,1}G_{W,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{W,m+1}$$
be the canonical inverse-image compositor (inverse to the direction in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]). Write $S_p$ for total derived system direct image, $J_j$ for exact system open extension, and $F=S_pJ_j:D(\mathscr S_X)\to D(\mathscr S_Y)$.

For each $r$, use the actual proper-adjunction mate and the open-adjunction comparison of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], item 2, with Frobenius replaced by its $r$-th power, to define
$$E_r=(S_p b_r)\circ(e_{p,r}J_j):G_{Y,r}F\longrightarrow FG_{X,r},$$
where $e_{p,r}:G_{Y,r}S_p\to S_pG_{\overline X,r}$ is the unit--square--counit mate and $b_r:G_{\overline X,r}J_j\to J_jG_{X,r}$ is the open-extension exchange, both formed in the system categories. Then for EVERY $C\in D(\mathscr S_X)$ and $m\geq1$ the following typed equation holds in $D(\mathscr S_Y)$:
$$E_{m+1,C}\circ t^Y_{m,FC}=F(t^X_{m,C})\circ E_{1,G_{X,m}C}\circ G_{Y,1}(E_{m,C}).$$
Both sides have source $G_{Y,1}G_{Y,m}FC$ and target $FG_{X,m+1}C$. The equation is natural in $C$ and is an identity of the simultaneous derived system transformations before evaluation or realization. No boundedness or finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on $C$ is needed. In the specialization $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, applying levelwise sections on $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ yields an equation of coefficient-complex towers. For general $Y$ the displayed equation remains an equation over $Y$ and makes no identification with $R\Gamma_c(X,-)$.

proof.text: Work throughout in the simultaneous system derived categories of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Abbreviate $G_r=G_{Y,r}$, $H_r=G_{\overline X,r}$, $K_r=G_{X,r}$, $S=S_p$, $J=J_j$ and $t=t^Y_m$, $u=t^{\overline X}_m$, $v=t^X_m$. The system adjunctions supply $P_p\dashv S$ and $J\dashv P_j$, where $P_a=a^{-1}$. Write $\theta_{a,r}:P_aG_{\mathrm{cod}(a),r}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\mathrm{dom}(a),r}P_a$ for the inverse-image square comparison, for $a=p,j$. Since $p,j$ descend to $k_0$, their compositions with the indicated Frobenius powers agree as scheme maps. By the recipe in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], $e_r=e_{p,r}$ is exactly the mate of $\theta_{p,r}$ and $E_r=(Sb_r)(e_rJ)$. These are the specified system transformations on every complex, rather than transformations reconstructed from their evaluations.

proof.text:
The square comparisons satisfy, for $a=p,j$, the compositor identity
$$\theta_{a,m+1}\,(P_at^{\mathrm{cod}(a)}_m)=(t^{\mathrm{dom}(a)}_mP_a)\,(G_{\mathrm{dom}(a),1}\theta_{a,m})\,(\theta_{a,1}G_{\mathrm{cod}(a),m}).$$
Here is the coherence check on the specified maps. On strict module systems, pullback composition is the canonical isomorphism of inverse-image left adjoints, along the constant-ring identifications. Direct images identify the corresponding composite sections by the canonical iterated base-change identifications; every route sends a section to the same section under the unique map of the iterated fibre product to the unparenthesized product. These identifications commute with the ring quotients and hence with every system transition. Taking the three successive adjunction Hom bijections gives the same Hom bijection for either parenthesization, by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] therefore makes both displayed paths the same comparison. This also checks the constant coefficient identifications: they are induced by pulling back constant sections and send each element to itself. Exact inverse images give the same equality on complexes. The simultaneous models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] preserve composition and the specified coherence, so the equality passes to $D(\mathscr S)$, with the compositors in the statement (the inverse direction to [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]). No equality of derived morphisms is inferred from equality at individual levels.

proof.text:
Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] with all three adjunctions $P_p\dashv S$, with $(G,H)=(G_m,H_m)$ and $(G_2,H_2)=(G_1,H_1)$. It identifies the mate of $(H_1\theta_{p,m})(\theta_{p,1}G_m)$ with $(e_1H_m)(G_1e_m)$. Step 2 identifies that left-adjoint square with $(uP_p)^{-1}\theta_{p,m+1}(P_pt)$. Taking mates and using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-whisker] to move $t$ and $u$ outside the mate gives
$$e_{m+1}\,(tS)=(Su)\,(e_1H_m)\,(G_1e_m).$$
In particular this is an identity of natural transformations $G_1G_mS\to SH_{m+1}$. No proper-base-change isomorphism theorem is used: the identity is for the actual unit--square--counit word, whether or not its components are invertible.

proof.text:
For the open factor put $a_r=b_r^{-1}:JK_r\to H_rJ$. The normalization of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], including its strict-system clause, says that $a_r$ is the $J\dashv P_j$ adjunct of $\theta_{j,r}^{-1}$ after insertion of the open unit: its transpose is $K_r\xrightarrow{K_r\eta}K_rP_jJ\xrightarrow{\theta_{j,r}^{-1}J}P_jH_rJ$. Equivalently its square mate under $J\dashv P_j$ on both sides is $\theta_{j,r}^{-1}$, by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to the $a_m,a_1$ squares. Their pasted left square is $(H_1a_m)(a_1K_m)$ and its mate is $(\theta_{j,1}^{-1}H_m)(K_1\theta_{j,m}^{-1})$. The inverse of Step 2 for $j$ identifies this with $(P_ju)^{-1}\theta_{j,m+1}^{-1}(vP_j)$. The mate bijection, with [lem-weil-pbc-mate-whisker] applied to its inverse direction, therefore gives
$$(H_1a_m)(a_1K_m)=(uJ)^{-1}a_{m+1}(Jv).$$
Inverting this equality and composing with $Jv$ and $uJ$ gives the required open identity
$$b_{m+1}\,(uJ)=(Jv)\,(b_1K_m)\,(H_1b_m).$$
All these operations are in the system categories. Invertibility is used only for the open exchange and the pullback compositors, both supplied by the cited constructions.

proof.text:
Substitute Steps 3 and 4 into $E_{m+1}(tSJ)$. Functoriality of $S$ gives
$$E_{m+1}(tSJ)=(SJv)(Sb_1K_m)(SH_1b_m)(e_1H_mJ)(G_1e_mJ).$$
Naturality of $e_1:G_1S\to SH_1$ at the actual morphism $b_{m,C}:H_mJC\to JK_mC$ gives
$$(SH_1b_m)(e_1H_mJ)=(e_1JK_m)(G_1Sb_m).$$
Replacing this adjacent pair and regrouping yields
$$E_{m+1}(tF)=F(v)(E_1K_m)(G_1E_m).$$
Its component at $C$ is precisely the equation in the statement. Every displayed substitution is between maps with the same endpoints, from $G_1G_mFC$ to $FK_{m+1}C$.

proof.text: The equality was obtained by functor composition, adjunction transposition and naturality on the simultaneous system models, all available for unbounded complexes by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. It is therefore natural in every $C\in D(\mathscr S_X)$ and precedes evaluation and realization. Applying the simultaneous derived sections operation on $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ when $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ preserves equality and gives the stated coefficient-complex tower equation. No inverse limit, boundedness argument, tensor reduction, or finite Tor-amplitude assertion enters the proof. For a general $Y$, the equality already has the displayed source and target over $Y$.
